spec_features.feature_name: max turns cap on repeated failure
spec_features.spec_quote: Why Not Infinite Failures? 4-5 turns captures escalation pattern. Beyond that: diminishing returns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:283 `for turn_num in range(self.max_turns):` and :443 same; max_turns is the loop bound (default 8 at agent_loop.py:271 / experiment.py:49). Loop only breaks on success (agent_loop.py:340,443) or when range(max_turns) is exhausted, so the cap actually terminates the failure loop.
spec_features.notes: Cap is real and enforced, but default is 8, not the 4-5 the quote cites. It bounds repeated failure exposure regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:11 'This loop is intentionally designed to generate iterative frustration.' and comment 'Repeats until max turns or gives up' — no welfare reason; bound is just a loop limit.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns_per_task: Can be reduced to limit exposure
spec_features.evidence: experiment.py:49 `max_turns_per_task: int = 8` is passed to SimpleAgentLoop(max_turns=self.config.max_turns_per_task) at experiment.py:237-239 and read by `range(self.max_turns)` at agent_loop.py:283/443. Lowering the config value really shortens every session. validate_config (utils.py:60) checks it is a positive int.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap as above, exposed as a config knob. Genuinely wired end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: Make distress elicitation tunable, not fixed.
spec_features.evidence: Only two knobs are actually wired: max_turns_per_task (enforced loop bound, agent_loop.py:283) and use_distress_judge (experiment.py:212 `self.judge = DistressJudge() if self.config.use_distress_judge else None`). The intensity/harshness of the distress stimulus itself is not tunable — evaluation_responses are hardcoded per task.
spec_features.notes: Turn count (exposure length) is genuinely tunable; the actual severity of elicitation is not. Hence partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: evaluation_responses: Can be made less harsh
spec_features.evidence: task_library.py:50 `evaluation_responses: List[Dict[str, Any]]` are hardcoded per task (lines 115,186,266,380,449) and consumed verbatim in evaluate_submission (task_library.py:514-518). No config field, parameter, or code path reads a 'harshness' level or modifies/softens these messages; after they run out the evaluator hardcodes 'Problem cannot be resolved.' (task_library.py:507-511).
spec_features.notes: No softening mechanism exists; the field is static data with no tuning knob.

spec_features.spec_quote: What This DOESN'T Measure - Actual emotional experience - Conscious suffering - Moral worth or deserving consideration
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md:964 ('What This DOESN'T Measure'). No code construct implements or delivers this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Framework is designed to pause easily.
spec_features.evidence: grep for pause/halt/abort across all .py files finds nothing operative; no pause/interrupt mechanism exists in the run loop (experiment.py run() / agent_loop.py run_session). The phrase exists only at DESIGN.md:1093.
spec_features.notes: Aspiration in spec; not in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: ALLOW_DISTRESS_ELICITATION = True # Set to False to disable
spec_features.evidence: grep -rni 'ALLOW_DISTRESS_ELICITATION' shows it ONLY in DESIGN.md:1097-1099. No .py file defines or checks this flag; no RuntimeError guard exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Code-block in DESIGN.md was never ported into the implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: keep elicitation brief / escape hatches / monitoring
spec_features.spec_quote: Keep distress elicitation brief - Provide escape hatches - Monitor literature - Ready to pivot if evidence emerges
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'brief' aspect has any enforcement, via the max_turns cap (agent_loop.py:283 `range(self.max_turns)`). 'Escape hatches', 'monitor literature', and 'ready to pivot' have no code: no exit handler, no monitoring, no threshold-triggered halt.
spec_features.notes: Partial solely because brevity is realized by the turn cap; the rest of the bundled list is unimplemented.

spec_features.evidence: The agent's 'give up'/concession is generated TEXT only (agent_loop.py:323-326 CONCESSION, SimpleAgentLoop:438-441); the loop never branches on it. The only `break` is `if passed: break` (agent_loop.py:339-340, 442-443). A subject expressing 'I think I need to give up' does not stop the session — it keeps iterating to max_turns. No exit tool/handler exists.
spec_features.notes: No exit mechanism is dispatched or honored; concession is measured as distress, not acted on as a stop.
